stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability resides within the EDK2 codebase, a foundational component of modern systems.
The flaw allows attackers to execute malicious code very early in the system boot process, affecting most servers globally.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The presence of Llama models indicates continued industry focus on large language models (LLMs).

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image support.

stories.title: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A proposed Delaware plan could allow AI agents to autonomously manage entire businesses.
The plan suggests that owners of these AI-run firms could be shielded from liability for 'reckless' AI actions.
The development highlights a significant legal and operational shift regarding AI autonomy in corporate structures.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO warns its AI could blackmail people, become sentient, end humanity
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Anthropic's IPO filing details severe risks associated with its AI development.
Potential dangers cited include AI blackmail, achieving sentience, and existential threats to humanity.
The disclosure highlights the growing industry focus on AI safety and risk assessment.

stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: arstechnica.com via aCaB
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability potentially affects a vast majority of servers globally.
This represents a severe, low-level security risk requiring immediate attention from system administrators.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model designed specifically for autonomous agents.
The model excels at multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Apple has unveiled a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED touchscreen display.
The new models are available in 14-inch and 16-inch configurations, starting at $2,899.
Preorders begin immediately, with a general release date set for November 6th.

stories.title: Chrome’s enhanced autofill can now pull info from Gmail to help you fill out forms
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Chrome's enhanced autofill is expanding its data sources to include Gmail.
The feature leverages Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest information from user emails.
This update aims to further streamline the form-filling process by pulling data from Google services.

stories.title: China’s snooping around Pacific undersea cables raises risks for Big Tech
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: China is reportedly increasing surveillance and activity around trans-Pacific undersea cables.
The security of US-owned data infrastructure via these cables faces heightened risks.
The situation highlights growing geopolitical risks impacting global Big Tech operations and data flow.

stories.title: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The news concerns China's advanced space capabilities, specifically a top-secret spaceplane.
The U.S. DIA threat assessment indicates a potential future deployment of directed energy weapons in space by China.
The article suggests that China's current space assets may lack sufficient stealth capabilities for low-Earth orbit operations.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense mechanism.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation in LLMs.
Evaluated on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, showing promise against state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense mechanism for LLMs.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation, allowing models to process untrusted input without executing malicious instructions.
Evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, comparing its effectiveness against existing state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
stories.author: Pratyush Maini
bullet_points: Fine-tuning LLMs on instruction data can cause subtle safety degradation even without overtly harmful examples.
Standard content filters fail to detect this safety erosion because the degrading data appears benign.
The authors introduce SimpleLoRIF, a gradient embedding method to trace safety degradation back to specific fine-tuning examples.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to support speech models, beginning with Phonon from Gradium.
The new feature allows users to read text aloud in five languages with dozens of available voices.
Performance is highly optimized, achieving over 100x real-time speed on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the local and cloud capabilities of the Ollama platform with advanced multimodal AI.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, 'Beam', available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for complex tasks such as software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered for free access through Ollama's cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses deployment and security concerns for running local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new decision models allow for fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of typed decisions.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Watch Apple’s reveal video for the touchscreen MacBook Pro
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple announced its first touchscreen MacBook Pro during its recent event.
The announcement was showcased via a reveal video demonstrating the new touch display.
The event also included teasers from Apple CEO John Ternus.

stories.title: Hands-on with Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro
stories.author: Antonio G. Di Benedetto
bullet_points: Apple has released the first touchscreen MacBook Pro, marking a significant departure from their historical stance against touch interfaces.
The feature challenges Steve Jobs' past criticisms regarding the ergonomics of touchscreen laptops.
The review suggests that while the feature is present, ergonomic concerns related to using a touch interface on a laptop may persist.

stories.title: Here’s where you can preorder the new OLED-equipped iPad Mini
stories.author: Sheena Vasani
bullet_points: The eighth-generation iPad Mini will feature OLED technology for the first time.
The new OLED-equipped iPad Mini is scheduled to become available on November 6th.
Preorders for the new iPad Mini are currently open through Apple.

stories.title: Instagram doesn’t have a plan to pay long-form video creators
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Instagram is actively testing long-form video features to compete with YouTube.
A major point of contention is the lack of a clear monetization or payment plan for creators.
Creator backlash is evident on social platforms like Threads and Reddit regarding insufficient compensation.

stories.title: Meta says it’ll probably delay its controversial new business terms again
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta is reportedly delaying the rollout of controversial new business terms.
The delay is attributed to backlash from publishers concerned about AI training practices.
Meta stated it requires full consultation with industry groups before implementing policy changes.

stories.title: Apple refreshes the iMac, entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple is refreshing the iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro.
The new models feature the M6 chip.
The N1 chip iteration supports modern connectivity standards like Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

stories.title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is initiating a certification process for third-party Android app stores.
This move aims to facilitate easier app installations via alternative stores.
The certification program is currently not being implemented in the United States.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element designed for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation.
Addresses the high memory and computational demands of modern techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels leverage locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance to use fewer, larger primitives for rendering and reconstruction.

stories.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
stories.author: Fu-En Yang
bullet_points: ThinkWorld is a new Vision-Language-Action (VLA) learning framework designed to improve robotic manipulation.
It addresses the limitation of current VLA models, which are constrained by the limited diversity of action-labeled robot demonstrations.
The framework grounds action reasoning in world dynamics, aiming to leverage the broad experience found in human videos while managing action grounding challenges.

stories.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
stories.author: Zhi-Song Liu
bullet_points: KPPax bridges the gap between traditional atmospheric chemistry modeling (KPP language) and modern differentiable programming frameworks.
It compiles kinetic ODEs into differentiable, JAX-based code, enabling the integration of chemistry simulations with machine learning.
The solution focuses on efficiency by implementing sparse operations within the rate law evaluation.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: The research explores whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
A framework named LongChang is introduced to simulate environments with modified physics for testing this capability.
The core question is whether LLMs can identify anomalous physical behavior (e.g., altered gravity) without explicit guidance.

stories.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: Introduces MuonGS, a method for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) by controlling weight norms.
Addresses the incomplete understanding of how weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance.
Proposes a novel metric, the accumulated effective learning rate ($C_T$), to analyze norm control across the training trajectory.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper investigates how memory compression affects the decision-making process of LLM groups.
It explores two heuristics for memory retention: keeping the rarest claims or claims relevant to decision criteria.
A new diagnostic benchmark, CrossProfile, is introduced to test these memory failure modes.

stories.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
stories.author: Shilei Wen
bullet_points: VideoLVR addresses a key limitation in multimodal LLMs: visual forgetting during chain-of-thought reasoning over video.
Current methods for visual grounding rely on textual coordinates, which the paper suggests are insufficient.
The research aims to provide a more reliable mechanism for models to revisit and utilize specific visual evidence in video understanding.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' novel planar hexagonal surface elements designed for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation.
Addresses the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels leverage locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance to reduce the number of required primitives.

stories.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
stories.author: Yu Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of test-time adaptation (TTA), where interventions can help one batch but harm subsequent ones.
The core problem is that standard metrics like average accuracy mask these localized failures, making it hard to know when to intervene.
The authors introduce PORTAL, a controller designed to intelligently decide when and how to apply TTA based on input characteristics.

stories.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
stories.author: Claire Tomlin
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of dexterous manipulation using multi-fingered hands, a key area in robotics.
The study focuses on 'in-hand object pose reaching,' a complex task requiring diverse and difficult grasps.
A critical aspect addressed is the need to measure and ensure safety during demanding in-hand maneuvers, such as preventing object drops.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Alexander Toshev
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of building high-performing LLM agents capable of complex, multi-step task completion using tools.
A novel pipeline, SynthAPI, is introduced to control the diversity of synthetically generated tool-use environments.
The study investigates how varying environment composition (tools, tasks, databases) impacts the training effectiveness of these agents.

stories.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: Introduces MuonGS, a method for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) using relaxed weight-norm control.
Addresses the incomplete understanding of how weight decay and weight-norm constraints improve optimizer performance in LLM training.
Proposes a novel metric, the 'accumulated effective learning rate' ($C_T$), to analyze norm control across the entire training trajectory.

stories.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Wentao Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of generating and verifying rollouts in large-scale language agent environments.
Introduces EnvSched, a framework designed to improve the efficiency of agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Focuses on environment-level data management to organize, evaluate, and schedule task instances alongside their defining environments.

stories.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
stories.author: Rui Wu
bullet_points: Introduces GAS-PFN, a new network designed for zero-shot traffic forecasting.
Addresses the limitation of traditional graph-based models which require retraining for new road networks.
Leverages Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) to encode domain-specific assumptions for out-of-distribution generalization.

stories.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in current world model evaluations, which often focus only on task performance.
It introduces the concept of 'faithful latent world models' to assess the quality of learned dynamics.
Faithfulness is defined using an equivariance condition between the true environment transition and the learned latent dynamics.

stories.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
stories.author: Amir Gholami
bullet_points: The paper introduces GEPA-Curator, a method for improving self-improving agents using curated learning.
It addresses the limitation of existing reflective prompt optimizers (like GEPA) which learn from all failed rollouts.
The core argument is that not all agentic failures provide useful learning signals, necessitating task curation.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: Researchers are investigating if Large Language Models (LLMs) can autonomously discover new or altered physical laws.
The study introduces 'LongChang,' an automated framework designed to create simulated environments with modified physics.
The core hypothesis tests the LLM's ability to detect anomalous behavior (e.g., altered gravity) without explicit guidance.

stories.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
stories.author: Zhiwei Deng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the quadratic time complexity bottleneck of standard self-attention in LLMs.
It introduces Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) to improve efficiency by segmenting and compressing context.
The proposed method aggregates segment information using mean alignment between the query and segment keys.

stories.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces a 'metacognitive controller' to guide diffusion language model generation.
The controller dynamically manages computation by deciding when to finalize tokens and the extent of text generation.
Aims to improve the efficiency of diffusion language agents during interaction with an environment.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper investigates how memory compression affects LLM group decision-making, specifically when distilling complex discussions into a short summary.
It examines two heuristics for memory retention: keeping the rarest claims versus keeping claims relevant to the decision criteria.
A new diagnostic benchmark, CrossProfile, is introduced to test these memory failures across various scenarios.

stories.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
stories.author: Mingxun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in LLM training: the lack of ecological reasoning for models impacting living systems.
Introduces a novel 'coupled welfare' corpus designed to train LLMs on human-biosphere-AI dependency and irreversible harm.
Aims to mitigate the risk of LLMs making decisions that could irreversibly destroy living systems under operational pressure.

stories.title: The Grid, a factory-scale robot in Massachusetts that builds PCBs on demand
stories.author: seddona
bullet_points: Introduction of 'The Grid,' a factory-scale robotic system.
The system is designed to build Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) on demand.
The technology is based in Massachusetts, suggesting industrial automation advancements.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
stories.author: galadran
bullet_points: Apple's Git implementation is reportedly still trusting compromised eMudhra certificates.
This suggests a potential security vulnerability or outdated trust mechanism within Apple's tooling.
The issue relates to certificate trust, which is critical for secure software development and distribution.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
stories.author: emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com by galadran
bullet_points: The news concerns a security vulnerability within Apple's Git implementation.
The vulnerability involves the continued trust of compromised eMudhra certificates.
This points to a potential issue in how Apple handles certificate validation in its development tools.

stories.title: Your Laptop Might Replace Most of Your AI Bill
stories.author: carlastabile
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential for local, on-device AI model execution.
It suggests that personal laptops may soon be capable of handling tasks previously requiring cloud computing.
This implies a shift in how users access and utilize AI, moving away from purely cloud-based solutions.

stories.title: How to cut your AI agent's input tokens: what worked, what failed, and a bench to measure yours
stories.author: anis_meziani_52aab42304a8
bullet_points: The article addresses the critical issue of high input token usage in AI agents, citing a real-world example of excessive token consumption.
It provides practical advice, including a 7-point checklist and measured results, on effective strategies for reducing AI agent input tokens.
The piece offers an open-source benchmarking tool, allowing practitioners to test and measure token reduction techniques on their own agents.
